candidates.name: penile squamous cell carcinoma
support_spans: a 2 × 2 cm irregular, friable mass on the glans
nearly complete epidermal ulceration with replacement by an in-situ and diffusely infiltrative atypical clear cell tumor
candidates.why: The patient presents with a lesion on the glans penis, which is consistent with penile squamous cell carcinoma.

candidates.name: extramammary Paget disease
support_spans: Within the epidermis, the cells displayed diffuse pagetoid spread
candidates.why: The presence of pagetoid spread within the epidermis is a characteristic feature of extramammary Paget disease.

candidates.name: clear-cell squamous cell carcinoma
support_spans: The tumor consisted of large irregular nests and lobules of clear cells with abundant multivacuolated cytoplasm, nuclear indentations, and vesicular to hyperchromatic nuclei
candidates.why: The tumor's histological features, including clear cells with multivacuolated cytoplasm, are consistent with clear-cell squamous cell carcinoma.

candidates.name: metastatic clear-cell carcinoma
support_spans: The initial differential diagnosis included a high-grade clear-cell squamous cell carcinoma and a metastatic clear-cell carcinoma
candidates.why: The patient's history of prostatic adenocarcinoma and the presence of lymphovascular invasion raise the possibility of metastatic clear-cell carcinoma.

candidates.name: primary penile squamous cell carcinoma
support_spans: A deep shave biopsy showed nearly complete epidermal ulceration with replacement by an in-situ and diffusely infiltrative atypical clear cell tumor
candidates.why: A definitive diagnosis of primary penile squamous cell carcinoma can be made based on the biopsy results.

candidates.name: metastatic renal cell carcinoma
support_spans: The tumor consisted of large irregular nests and lobules of clear cells with abundant multivacuolated cytoplasm, nuclear indentations, and vesicular to hyperchromatic nuclei
candidates.why: The histological features of the tumor are also consistent with metastatic renal cell carcinoma, which can be confirmed with immunohistochemistry or other diagnostic tests.
